name: Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals
note: Microsoft scores AI-901 on a 1–1000 scale with 700 to pass. This practice exam reports a straight percentage; treat 80% as your readiness bar. Questions follow the skills measured as of April 15, 2026. Foundry features and SDKs change quickly, so check current names and code on Microsoft Learn.

domains.name: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry

questions.stem: A loan-approval model approves applicants from one ethnic group at a much lower rate than equally qualified applicants from other groups. Which responsible AI principle is most at risk?
questions.explanation: Fairness means AI systems should treat all people fairly and avoid allocating opportunities, resources, or information differently to similar people. Biased approval rates are a classic fairness problem, often caused by biased training data.

questions.stem: Which practice best helps an AI team address fairness?
options: Adding more GPUs to reduce response latency
Publishing the model's source code on GitHub
Encrypting the training data while it's at rest
questions.explanation: Checking whether error rates and outcomes differ across groups reveals unfair behavior so it can be mitigated, for example by rebalancing training data. Encryption supports privacy, and publishing code or adding compute doesn't address bias.

questions.stem: An AI system that helps diagnose medical images must perform consistently and fail safely when it encounters unusual inputs. Which principle does this describe?
questions.explanation: Reliability and safety means AI systems should perform as intended, respond safely to unanticipated conditions, and resist harmful manipulation. Rigorous testing, monitoring, and human review of edge cases support it.

questions.stem: Before releasing a generative AI chatbot, a team tests it against adversarial prompts designed to make it produce harmful content. Which principle does this testing primarily support?
questions.explanation: Red-teaming with adversarial prompts checks that the system behaves safely under misuse, which is part of reliability and safety. Content filters and guardrails help mitigate the risks it uncovers.

questions.stem: A company's AI solution processes customer conversations. Which consideration falls under the privacy and security principle?
options: Explaining to users how the model reaches its conclusions
Protecting personal data and access to it
Designing the app to work with screen readers
Making sure the model performs equally well for all users
questions.explanation: Privacy and security covers protecting personal and business data, respecting consent and data-use rules, and securing the system against misuse. Equal performance is fairness, explanation is transparency, and accessibility is inclusiveness.

questions.stem: Which technique supports privacy when training or evaluating AI models on customer data?
options: Publishing the full dataset for outside review
Removing or masking personal information first
Training on more data from the same customers
questions.explanation: Detecting and redacting personally identifiable information (PII) before data is used reduces privacy risk. Azure Language PII detection can help with this. Temperature affects randomness, and publishing data would harm privacy.

questions.stem: A speech-enabled app is designed so that people with speech impairments, strong accents, or limited mobility can all use it effectively. Which principle does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Inclusiveness means AI systems should empower and engage everyone, including people with disabilities, by considering a wide range of users and abilities during design.

questions.stem: Which design choice best supports inclusiveness?
options: Restricting the app to users of a single language
Choosing the model with the highest benchmark score
Involving people with diverse abilities in testing
Logging every request for later audit and review
questions.explanation: Inclusive design involves a diverse range of people, including people with disabilities, in design and testing so the system works for them. Auditing supports accountability, and benchmark scores don't measure inclusiveness.

questions.stem: Users of an AI hiring tool are told that AI is involved, what data it uses, and what its limitations are. Which principle does this support?
questions.explanation: Transparency means people should understand how and why an AI system is used and its capabilities and limitations. Disclosing AI involvement and documenting intended uses, such as in a transparency note, supports it.

questions.stem: Microsoft publishes documents describing each AI service's intended uses, capabilities, and limitations. Which principle do these documents mainly support?
questions.explanation: Transparency notes help customers understand how a service works, what it's designed for, and where it may fall short, so they can deploy it responsibly.

questions.stem: An organization assigns a review board to approve high-risk AI deployments and remain answerable for their outcomes. Which principle does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Accountability means the people who design and deploy AI systems are responsible for how they operate. Governance structures such as review boards, policies, and human oversight put that responsibility into practice.

questions.stem: Which statement reflects the accountability principle?
options: The AI system should work for people of all abilities
The people deploying it stay responsible for its outcomes
The AI system must give identical results to every user
The model's training data must be shared with all of its users
questions.explanation: Under accountability, humans stay responsible for AI systems and their impact, with oversight and the ability to intervene. Results that work for everyone relate to fairness and inclusiveness.

questions.stem: How does a large language model generate a response?
options: It follows hand-written rules that developers created for each topic
It repeatedly predicts the next token from learned patterns
It looks up a stored answer for each question in a large database
It runs a search engine query and returns the top-ranked web page
questions.explanation: A large language model is trained on vast amounts of text to learn statistical relationships between tokens. At inference time, it generates output one token at a time, each time predicting a likely next token given everything before it.

questions.stem: What is a token in the context of a language model?
options: A unit of text, such as a word or word part
A password that authenticates calls to the model
A full sentence that the model has memorized
A single training example in the dataset
questions.explanation: Models split text into tokens — whole words, parts of words, or punctuation — and process and bill by token count. An API key or access token for authentication is a different meaning of the word.

questions.stem: What are embeddings?
options: Images that a model inserts into its generated text responses
Vectors of numbers that represent meaning
Hidden instructions added to every prompt by the service
Compressed copies of the training data stored in the model
questions.explanation: Embeddings map text (or other content) to vectors in a multidimensional space where semantically similar items are close together. They power semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation.

questions.stem: Which part of the transformer architecture lets a model weigh how much each token in the input relates to the others?
questions.explanation: Attention lets the model consider relationships between all tokens in the context, so meaning is interpreted in context — for example, which noun a pronoun refers to. The tokenizer only splits text into tokens.

questions.stem: What is a model's context window?
options: The time limit for a single request before the model stops responding
The most tokens it can handle in one request, including output
The range of dates covered by the model's training data
The browser window where users chat with the deployed model
questions.explanation: The context window limits how many tokens — system message, conversation history, retrieved data, and the response — fit in a single call. Longer conversations may need summarizing or trimming to fit.

questions.stem: A generative AI app sometimes states incorrect facts confidently. What is this behavior called?
questions.explanation: Hallucination is when a model produces fluent but false or unsupported content. Grounding responses in trusted data, such as with retrieval-augmented generation, and instructing the model to say when it doesn't know help reduce it.

questions.stem: What does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) do?
options: Retrains the model on new data every time a user asks a question
Adds retrieved data to the prompt to ground answers
Generates synthetic training data to make the model larger
Compresses the model so it can run on a mobile device offline
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant content, often by vector search over embeddings, and includes it in the prompt so the model answers from that data. It doesn't change the model's weights, unlike fine-tuning.

questions.stem: When is fine-tuning a better choice than prompt engineering or RAG?
options: When the model needs facts that change daily, such as prices
When you want to avoid preparing any training examples at all
When you need answers to cite the source documents they used
When you need a consistent style that prompts can't achieve
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning further trains a model on examples to teach a consistent format, tone, or specialized behavior. For frequently changing facts or citations, RAG is better, since it uses current data at query time. Fine-tuning requires prepared training data.

questions.stem: A team needs a model that can solve multi-step math and logic problems, and a slower response is acceptable. Which type of model fits best?
questions.explanation: Reasoning models spend extra computation working through problems step by step before answering, which improves results on complex math, logic, and planning tasks at the cost of latency and tokens.

questions.stem: An app must run a language model on low-cost hardware with fast responses for simple tasks. Which type of model is most appropriate?
options: A small language model, such as Phi
questions.explanation: Small language models such as Microsoft's Phi family trade some capability for lower cost, lower latency, and the ability to run on modest or local hardware — a good fit for simpler, well-scoped tasks.

questions.stem: Which kind of model should you choose to answer questions about a photo that a user uploads?
questions.explanation: Multimodal models, such as GPT-4o and later GPT models, accept images along with text in the prompt and can describe or reason about them. Text-only, embedding, and speech models can't interpret the image.

questions.stem: Where in Microsoft Foundry can you compare models by quality, cost, and throughput before choosing one?
options: The Azure Cost Management budgets page
questions.explanation: The Foundry model catalog includes benchmark and leaderboard views that compare models on quality, safety, cost, and performance, plus model cards describing capabilities. Budgets and activity logs don't compare models.

questions.stem: What does the temperature parameter control?
options: How many past messages are included
Which model version handles the request
The maximum length of the response
questions.explanation: Lower temperature makes outputs more focused and deterministic, while higher temperature makes them more varied and creative. Response length is set by a maximum-token setting, and history depends on what your app sends.

questions.stem: A chatbot's answers keep getting cut off midway through. Which parameter should you check first?
questions.explanation: The maximum output tokens setting caps response length, so a low value truncates answers. Temperature and top-p affect randomness, and frequency penalty discourages repeated tokens.

questions.stem: An organization needs high, predictable throughput for a model deployment with reserved capacity. Which deployment type fits?
options: A batch deployment for offline jobs
A local deployment on one laptop
questions.explanation: Provisioned deployments reserve model processing capacity (measured in provisioned throughput units) for consistent latency and throughput. Standard deployments are pay-per-token, and batch deployments process large asynchronous jobs at lower cost.

questions.stem: A company must keep data processing for its model deployment within the EU while still benefiting from Microsoft's capacity across multiple EU regions. Which deployment type fits?
questions.explanation: Data Zone deployments route traffic across regions within a defined geography, such as the EU or US, balancing data-residency requirements with available capacity. Global deployments can process data in any Azure region.

questions.stem: An app automatically writes first drafts of marketing emails from a short description. Which AI workload is this?
questions.explanation: Generative AI creates new content — text, images, code, or audio — from a prompt. The other workloads analyze existing input rather than producing new content.

questions.stem: What distinguishes an AI agent from a simple chatbot?
options: It can only respond with prewritten text answers
It can plan and act using tools to complete tasks
It never uses a large language model to respond
It runs only on a user's device, without the cloud
questions.explanation: Agents combine a model with instructions and tools — such as search, code execution, or APIs — so they can reason about a goal, take actions, and use the results. A simple chatbot only generates replies.

questions.stem: A support system automatically reads customer reviews and labels each as positive, negative, or neutral. Which workload is this?
questions.explanation: Determining the opinion expressed in text is sentiment analysis, a text analysis (natural language processing) workload.

questions.stem: A system converts recorded phone calls into searchable transcripts. Which workload is this?
questions.explanation: Speech recognition (speech to text) converts spoken audio into text. Speech synthesis does the reverse, turning text into spoken audio.

questions.stem: A warehouse camera system counts packages on a conveyor belt and locates each one in the frame. Which workload is this?
questions.explanation: Computer vision interprets images and video. Locating and counting items with bounding boxes is object detection, a computer vision task.

questions.stem: An insurer needs to pull policy numbers, claim amounts, and dates from thousands of submitted forms into a database. Which workload is this?
questions.explanation: Information extraction turns unstructured content, such as forms, documents, images, audio, or video, into structured fields that systems can use. Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools is designed for this.

questions.stem: Which text analysis technique identifies the main talking points in a document, such as "battery life" and "screen quality"?
questions.explanation: Key phrase extraction returns the important phrases in text, summarizing what it's about. Language detection identifies the language, and sentiment analysis measures opinion.

questions.stem: Which technique identifies people, places, organizations, and dates mentioned in text?
questions.explanation: Named entity recognition (NER) finds references to entities and classifies them into categories such as person, location, organization, and date/time. Entity linking can also connect them to a knowledge base.

questions.stem: What does sentiment analysis return for a piece of text?
options: A shorter version that covers the main points
The language the text is written in, with a confidence
Positive, negative, neutral, or mixed opinion
A list of the people and places that are mentioned
questions.explanation: Sentiment analysis labels text positive, negative, neutral, or mixed, with confidence scores, at the document and sentence level. Opinion mining can go further, tying sentiment to specific aspects such as "service" or "price".

questions.stem: What is the difference between extractive and abstractive summarization?
options: Extractive writes new sentences; abstractive picks key sentences
They're the same technique under two different names
Extractive works on audio; abstractive works only on text
Extractive selects sentences; abstractive writes new ones
questions.explanation: Extractive summarization selects the most important sentences from the original text. Abstractive summarization generates new text that conveys the main ideas, which is how generative models usually summarize.

questions.stem: A company must find and redact Social Security numbers and phone numbers in support tickets. Which capability fits?
questions.explanation: PII detection identifies personally identifiable information, such as phone numbers, email addresses, and government IDs, and can return redacted text.

questions.stem: A global help desk needs to route incoming messages to agents who speak the same language as the customer. Which technique fits first?
questions.explanation: Language detection identifies the language of the text, along with a confidence score, so the message can be routed correctly or translated.

questions.stem: What does speech synthesis do?
options: Identifies who is speaking in audio
questions.explanation: Speech synthesis (text to speech) generates spoken audio from text, typically using natural-sounding neural voices. Speech recognition converts audio into text.

questions.stem: An app needs to control the pronunciation, speaking rate, and pauses of synthesized speech. What should it use?
options: A custom keyword list for recognition
A higher temperature for the speech model
questions.explanation: SSML is an XML-based markup that controls how text is spoken, including voice, pitch, rate, pauses, and pronunciation. Diarization and keyword lists relate to speech recognition.

questions.stem: A meeting transcription service must label which participant said each sentence. Which speech capability provides this?
questions.explanation: Diarization separates speakers in audio so the transcript shows who spoke when, such as "Speaker 1" and "Speaker 2".

questions.stem: A traveler speaks English into an app, and the app outputs the same sentence as spoken Spanish. Which capability is this?
questions.explanation: Speech translation recognizes speech in one language and translates it into text or synthesized speech in another language.

questions.stem: Which speech recognition setting improves accuracy for product names and industry terms that the base model often gets wrong?
options: A phrase list or custom speech model
A different neural voice for output
A higher speaking rate in SSML
questions.explanation: Phrase lists give the recognizer hints about specific words, and custom speech models trained on your data handle specialized vocabulary or acoustic conditions. SSML and voices affect synthesis, not recognition.

questions.stem: Which computer vision task returns a sentence describing what's happening in an image?
questions.explanation: Captioning generates a human-readable description of an image. Object detection locates objects with bounding boxes, OCR reads text, and classification assigns a label to the whole image.

questions.stem: What's the difference between image classification and object detection?
options: They're the same task with different output formats
Classification reads text; detection describes the overall scene
Classification labels the image; detection locates objects
Classification locates each object; detection labels the whole image
questions.explanation: Image classification predicts what the image as a whole contains. Object detection identifies individual objects and returns a bounding box for each, so it can count and locate them.

questions.stem: Which capability reads printed and handwritten text from photos of signs and documents?
questions.explanation: OCR extracts text from images, including printed and handwritten text. Captioning describes the scene but doesn't transcribe the text exactly.

questions.stem: A design team wants to create original product illustrations from text descriptions. Which kind of model fits?
questions.explanation: Image-generation models, such as GPT-image models available in Foundry, create new images from text prompts, and some can edit existing images. The other models analyze images rather than create them.

questions.stem: Why do services that analyze faces restrict some capabilities, such as identification, to approved customers?
options: Because those features need special camera hardware
Because face analysis models can't run in the cloud
To lower the cost of running the face models for everyone
To reduce misuse, such as unwanted surveillance
questions.explanation: Microsoft limits access to sensitive facial recognition features under its responsible AI commitments, because they can be misused for surveillance or to harm privacy. Customers must apply and meet use-case requirements.

questions.stem: A company wants structured data from invoices, product photos, recorded support calls, and training videos using one service. Which Foundry tool fits?
questions.explanation: Content Understanding processes documents, images, audio, and video, extracting content and schema-defined fields from each. Speech and Translator handle single modalities, and AI Search indexes content for retrieval.

questions.stem: An organization wants a summary and the main topics from each hour-long recorded webinar. Which workload covers this?
options: Extracting information from video and audio
Detecting the language of short messages
Generating new images from text prompts
questions.explanation: Information extraction from audio and video transcribes speech, analyzes visual content, and can generate fields such as summaries, topics, or scene descriptions — something Content Understanding supports.

questions.stem: Which technique converts a scanned paper form into structured key-value pairs, such as "Name: Jane Doe"?
questions.explanation: Document field extraction combines OCR and layout analysis with models that find the values for defined fields, returning structured key-value data rather than plain text.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the system message (instructions) in a chat app?
options: To store the user's previous questions for the next session
To choose which model deployment handles each request
To authenticate the app with the Foundry project
To set the model's role, behavior, and limits
questions.explanation: The system message, or instructions, tells the model who it is, how to respond, and what to avoid — for example, "You're a support assistant for Contoso. Answer only questions about Contoso products." User messages carry each request.

questions.stem: A prompt includes three sample customer emails, each followed by the ideal one-line category. What is this technique called?
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting includes example inputs and desired outputs in the prompt so the model follows the pattern. Zero-shot gives no examples, and fine-tuning changes the model through training.

questions.stem: A chatbot answers questions from a provided policy document but sometimes invents details. Which instruction is most likely to help?
options: "Be as creative and detailed as you can in every answer."
"Use only the provided document; say if it isn't there."
"Use your general knowledge to fill in any missing details."
"Answer quickly, using as few words as possible."
questions.explanation: Telling the model to rely only on the supplied context and to admit when it doesn't know reduces ungrounded answers. Encouraging creativity or general knowledge makes invented details more likely.

questions.stem: An app needs the model's output in a consistent JSON format that code can parse. What should the prompt do?
options: Raise the temperature so the output varies more
Specify the exact JSON structure, with an example
Remove the system message so the model isn't constrained
Ask the model to respond in any format it prefers
questions.explanation: Spelling out the required fields and format, with an example, makes output predictable. Many models also support structured outputs that enforce a JSON schema. Higher temperature makes output less consistent.

questions.stem: A complex request produces muddled answers. Which prompt technique often improves results?
options: Breaking the task into clear, ordered steps
Removing all the context about the task
Shortening the prompt to a single word
Repeating the same request several times
questions.explanation: Splitting a complex task into explicit steps, or asking the model to work through it step by step, helps it handle each part. Removing context or repeating requests doesn't add clarity.

questions.stem: Which user prompt is most likely to produce a useful result?
options: "Tell me something about this report, whatever you like."
"Summarize this in three bullets for executives."
"Make this report better somehow, in any way you want."
questions.explanation: Effective prompts are specific about the task, format, length, and audience. Vague prompts leave the model guessing about what you want.

questions.stem: Why does a chat app send earlier messages, or a conversation ID, with each new request?
options: The model itself doesn't remember earlier requests
The model needs them to authenticate the user
Each message must be sent twice to be accepted
The service charges less for longer requests
questions.explanation: Models are stateless between calls, so context must be supplied each time — either by resending history or by referencing a conversation the service stores. That's how follow-up questions like "And what's its capital?" make sense.

questions.stem: What do you typically need to do before your app can call a model from your Foundry project?
options: Deploy it and call it by its deployment name
Register the model in Microsoft Entra ID as a user
Download the model's weights to the app's server
Fine-tune the model on your own company data
questions.explanation: You deploy a model from the catalog to your Foundry resource, giving the deployment a name, and your code references that name. Downloading weights and fine-tuning aren't required to use a model.

questions.stem: Where can you chat with a deployed model and adjust its instructions and parameters without writing code?
options: The playground in the Foundry portal
questions.explanation: The Foundry portal's playground lets you try a deployment, edit instructions, and tune parameters such as temperature, and it can show sample code for the same request.

questions.stem: You deployed gpt-5-mini under the deployment name "support-model". In your code, what value goes in the model parameter?
questions.explanation: Requests reference the deployment name you chose. If you deployed a model under a different name than the model itself, use that deployment name in code.

questions.stem: What do guardrails, such as content filters, on a Foundry model deployment do?
options: Limit how many tokens each user can send per day
Encrypt the prompts while they're stored at rest
Translate prompts into English before processing
Detect and block harmful prompts and outputs
questions.explanation: Guardrails classify inputs and outputs for categories such as hate, violence, sexual content, and self-harm, and can detect jailbreak attempts, blocking or annotating content based on configured severity thresholds.

questions.stem: Before releasing an app, a team wants to measure the groundedness, relevance, and safety of its responses on a test dataset. What should it use in Foundry?
questions.explanation: Foundry evaluations run your app or model against test data and score outputs with evaluators for quality (such as groundedness, relevance, and coherence) and for safety risks.

questions.stem: Which Python package provides the AIProjectClient class for working with a Foundry project?
questions.explanation: The azure-ai-projects package (the Foundry SDK) provides AIProjectClient. Text analytics, Speech, and Blob Storage have their own packages.

questions.stem: Which endpoint format does AIProjectClient use?
questions.explanation: A Foundry project endpoint has the form https://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project-name>, shown on the project's overview page.

questions.stem: A developer signed in with az login. Which credential should the app pass to AIProjectClient to use that sign-in, without storing keys?
questions.explanation: DefaultAzureCredential, from azure-identity, tries several sources in turn — environment variables, managed identity, and developer sign-ins such as the Azure CLI — so the same code works locally and in Azure without keys in code.

questions.stem: After creating an AIProjectClient named project, how do you get a client for calling a deployed model?
questions.explanation: get_openai_client() returns an OpenAI-compatible client that's already configured for the project, so you can call APIs such as responses.create.

questions.stem: Which call sends a prompt to a deployed model and returns a response with an output_text property?
questions.explanation: The Responses API call responses.create takes the deployment name and input, and the returned response exposes the generated text as output_text.

questions.stem: How can a Foundry SDK client keep context across multiple turns without resending the whole history itself?
options: Raise the max tokens so the model remembers more
Create a new AIProjectClient for every message
Create a conversation and pass its ID each time
Store the history in the system message manually
questions.explanation: openai.conversations.create() creates a conversation, and passing conversation=conversation.id to responses.create lets the service keep the history, so follow-up questions have context.

questions.stem: Which components define a basic agent in Foundry Agent Service?
options: A model, instructions, and optional tools
A database, a web server, and a firewall
A training dataset and a fine-tuning job
A speech voice, a language, and a region
questions.explanation: An agent combines a deployed model with instructions that define its behavior, plus tools that let it retrieve knowledge or take actions.

questions.stem: An agent must answer questions using the company's uploaded HR policy PDFs. Which tool should you add?
questions.explanation: File search indexes uploaded files into a vector store so the agent can retrieve relevant passages and ground its answers in them.

questions.stem: An agent must analyze an uploaded CSV file and produce a chart of monthly sales. Which tool should you add?
questions.explanation: Code interpreter lets the agent write and run Python in a sandbox to analyze data, do calculations, and create files such as charts.

questions.stem: An agent must look up live order status in the company's own REST API. Which kind of tool fits?
questions.explanation: OpenAPI tools and function calling let an agent call external APIs or your own code with structured arguments, so it can fetch live data or take actions. Uploaded files would be out of date.

questions.stem: An agent must answer questions about today's news. Which tool gives it current public information?
questions.explanation: Web search grounding, such as Grounding with Bing Search, retrieves current public web results and lets the agent cite them. A model's built-in knowledge stops at its training cutoff.

questions.stem: In the Foundry SDK for Python, which call creates an agent from a model and instructions?
questions.explanation: agents.create_version takes an agent name and a definition, such as PromptAgentDefinition(model=..., instructions=...), and returns the agent's name, ID, and version.

questions.stem: How does a Python client send a message to an existing agent named "MyAgent"?
options: Call responses.create on a client bound to the agent
Write the message to a storage queue the agent watches
Open the agent's playground URL in a headless browser
Call the agent's model deployment with no instructions
questions.explanation: project.get_openai_client(agent_name="MyAgent") returns a client bound to that agent. Calling responses.create, optionally with a conversation ID, runs the agent with its instructions and tools.

questions.stem: You call agents.create_version for an agent name that already exists. What happens?
options: A second agent with a numbered name appears
A new version of that agent is created
The existing agent is deleted permanently
The call fails because the name is taken
questions.explanation: Agents are versioned: creating a version for an existing name adds a new version with the updated definition, which keeps a history of changes.

questions.stem: Which Python client calls Azure Language text analysis features such as sentiment and key phrases?
questions.explanation: The azure-ai-textanalytics package provides TextAnalyticsClient, with methods for sentiment, key phrases, entities, PII, language detection, and summarization.

questions.stem: What do you need to create a TextAnalyticsClient?
options: Its endpoint plus a key or token
An SSML document and a voice name
The model's training data and a GPU
A Foundry agent name and a conversation ID
questions.explanation: Like other Foundry Tools clients, TextAnalyticsClient takes the resource's endpoint plus a credential — an AzureKeyCredential with a key, or a Microsoft Entra token credential.

questions.stem: Which TextAnalyticsClient method returns positive, negative, neutral, or mixed labels for each document?
questions.explanation: analyze_sentiment returns a sentiment label and confidence scores for each document and its sentences.

questions.stem: Which TextAnalyticsClient method identifies the language of each input document?
questions.explanation: detect_language returns the primary language of each document, such as English or French, with an ISO code and confidence score.

questions.stem: An app must return support tickets with phone numbers and email addresses masked. Which method's result includes redacted text?
questions.explanation: recognize_pii_entities returns the PII entities found and a redacted_text version of each document with them masked.

questions.stem: An app must accept a spoken question and answer it directly, without a separate speech-to-text step. What should it use?
options: A text embedding model with a vector index
An image-generation model with a voice prompt
A deployed multimodal model that accepts audio input
questions.explanation: Audio-capable multimodal models, such as GPT-4o audio models, can take spoken input and respond in text or speech, so the app doesn't need to transcribe first.

questions.stem: A voice assistant needs low-latency, back-and-forth spoken conversation that users can interrupt. Which option fits best?
options: An embedding model with a speech plugin
A realtime audio model through the Realtime API
An image-generation model with audio output
A batch deployment that processes audio overnight
questions.explanation: Realtime models, such as gpt-realtime, stream audio in and out over a persistent connection for natural, low-latency speech conversations. Batch processing is for offline jobs.

questions.stem: How is a recorded audio clip typically included in a chat request to an audio-capable model?
options: As a link to a public video sharing website
As a list of phonemes typed by the user
As base64-encoded audio in the message
As SSML markup inside the system message
questions.explanation: Audio input is typically sent as an audio content part containing base64-encoded data and its format, such as WAV or MP3, alongside any text in the message.

questions.stem: Which Python package provides the Azure Speech SDK?
questions.explanation: The Speech SDK for Python is installed as azure-cognitiveservices-speech and is usually imported as azure.cognitiveservices.speech.

questions.stem: In the Speech SDK, which object holds the key and region (or endpoint) plus settings such as the recognition language?
questions.explanation: SpeechConfig holds the connection details and service settings, such as speech_recognition_language and speech_synthesis_voice_name. AudioConfig specifies the audio input or output, such as a microphone or file.

questions.stem: Which Speech SDK class transcribes speech from a microphone or audio file?
questions.explanation: SpeechRecognizer performs speech to text using a SpeechConfig and an AudioConfig. SpeechSynthesizer performs text to speech.

questions.stem: Which Speech SDK class converts text into spoken audio?
questions.explanation: SpeechSynthesizer generates audio from text with methods such as speak_text_async, or speak_ssml_async for SSML input, playing it to a speaker or writing it to a file.

questions.stem: How do you choose which neural voice the Speech SDK uses for synthesis?
options: Upload a recording of the voice to the project
Pass the voice name as the recognition language
Set the voice name on the SpeechConfig
Choose the voice in Azure Monitor settings
questions.explanation: Setting speech_synthesis_voice_name, for example to "en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural", selects a prebuilt neural voice. SSML can also set the voice per request.

questions.stem: After calling recognize_once_async().get(), how does the app confirm that speech was successfully transcribed?
options: Check that the HTTP status code returned is 404
Check that result.text equals the SSML input
Check that the audio file was deleted afterward
questions.explanation: The result's reason indicates the outcome: RecognizedSpeech means result.text holds the transcript, NoMatch means speech couldn't be recognized, and Canceled indicates an error.

questions.stem: An app must transcribe a 30-minute recorded lecture. Which Speech SDK approach fits?
questions.explanation: recognize_once returns after a single utterance, ending at a pause or after about 15 seconds. Continuous recognition processes speech until you stop it, raising events as phrases are recognized. Large batches of files can also use batch transcription.

questions.stem: How do you include an image in a Responses API request to a multimodal model?
options: Upload the image to the model catalog before the call
Add an input_image item with a URL or data
Put the image file name inside the system message text
Set the temperature to a value above 1.0 for images
questions.explanation: The input can be a list of content items: an input_text item with the question and an input_image item whose image_url is a web URL or a base64 data URL.

questions.stem: An app needs to send a local photo, which isn't on the web, to a multimodal model. How should it send the image?
options: As a description typed by the user
As an attachment in an email
As the photo's file path on disk
questions.explanation: The service can't read files on your machine, so the app reads the image, base64-encodes it, and sends it as a data URL such as data:image/jpeg;base64,....

questions.stem: Which prompt is most likely to get usable data from a photo of a receipt sent to a multimodal model?
options: "What do you think of this picture?"
"Describe the image in as much detail as possible."
"Return the store name, date, and total as JSON."
questions.explanation: Specific instructions about which fields to return and in what format make the output predictable and easy for code to use.

questions.stem: A multimodal model is used to read part numbers from photos of equipment labels. What's a sensible safeguard?
options: Lower the image resolution so the model reads it faster
Assume every value is correct because the model is multimodal
Validate critical values, since models can misread details
Remove the instructions so the model can decide what to do
questions.explanation: Multimodal models can misread small or blurry text or miscount objects, so important values should be validated, for example with format checks or human review.

questions.stem: Which model in the Foundry catalog generates images from text prompts?
questions.explanation: GPT-image models generate and edit images from text prompts. text-embedding-3-large creates embeddings, Whisper transcribes speech, and Phi-4-mini is a small language model.

questions.stem: What usually makes an image-generation prompt more effective?
options: Asking the model to surprise you with anything
Describing the subject, style, and lighting
Keeping the prompt to a single vague word
Repeating the same word many times
questions.explanation: Detailed prompts that describe what to show, the visual style, framing, and mood give the model clear direction and produce results closer to what you want.

questions.stem: A team wants to replace the background of an existing product photo while keeping the product unchanged. What should it use?
options: A text embedding of the product description
A speech synthesis request describing it
An image edit request with the original image
An OCR call to read the product's label
questions.explanation: Image-generation models such as gpt-image-1 support edits: you supply the original image, a prompt describing the change, and optionally a mask marking the area to change.

questions.stem: A user's image-generation request is rejected with a content policy error. What's the most likely cause?
options: The guardrails flagged the prompt as harmful
The model needs fine-tuning before it can draw anything
The prompt was written in a language other than English
The deployment ran out of disk space for images
questions.explanation: Guardrails screen image prompts and generated images for harmful content and block requests that violate policy. Prompts in many languages are supported.

questions.stem: Which Python client analyzes images with Azure Vision in Foundry Tools to return captions, tags, objects, and text?
questions.explanation: ImageAnalysisClient's analyze method takes an image and a list of visual features, such as CAPTION, TAGS, OBJECTS, and READ, and returns results for each.

questions.stem: Which visual feature should you request from Image Analysis to extract printed and handwritten text?
questions.explanation: The READ feature performs OCR, returning lines and words of text with their positions. CAPTION describes the scene, TAGS lists content keywords, and SMART_CROPS suggests thumbnail regions.

questions.stem: Which visual feature returns bounding boxes for items such as cars and bicycles in an image?
questions.explanation: OBJECTS performs object detection, returning each detected object's name, confidence, and bounding box. TAGS lists content keywords without locations.

questions.stem: When might an app use Image Analysis rather than prompting a multimodal model?
options: When it needs to generate a brand-new image from text
When it needs fast, consistent tags, boxes, and text
When it needs an open-ended conversation about the image
When it needs to explain its reasoning in detail
questions.explanation: Image Analysis returns predictable, structured results for specific tasks at low latency. Multimodal models are more flexible for open-ended questions and reasoning about images.

questions.stem: In Azure Content Understanding, what defines how content is processed and which fields are returned?
questions.explanation: An analyzer configures content extraction settings, the field schema, and the model deployments to use, and applies them consistently to every file it processes. Content Understanding offers prebuilt analyzers and custom ones.

questions.stem: A company needs fields that are specific to its own internal application form. What should it create in Content Understanding?
options: A new prebuilt analyzer from Microsoft
A custom analyzer with its own field schema
A speech-to-text model for the form
A separate Foundry resource per field
questions.explanation: Custom analyzers let you define your own fields, their types, descriptions, and methods. Prebuilt analyzers cover common scenarios such as invoices.

questions.stem: A field must return the invoice date exactly as it's printed on the document. Which field method fits?
questions.explanation: Extract returns values as they appear in the input content and is supported for documents. Generate creates values freely, such as summaries, and Classify chooses from predefined categories.

questions.stem: A field should contain a short summary of each recorded support call. Which field method fits?
questions.explanation: Generate produces values from the input data that don't appear verbatim, such as summaries of audio conversations or scene descriptions of videos.

questions.stem: A field must label each incoming document as "invoice", "receipt", or "contract". Which field method fits?
questions.explanation: Classify assigns a value from a predefined set of categories, such as document type or call sentiment. Classification can also route content to the right analyzer.

questions.stem: An automated workflow must decide when an extracted value needs human review. Which Content Understanding outputs help most?
options: The confidence score and grounding for each field
The name of the model deployment that was used
The total number of pages in the input document
The time the analyzer was originally created
questions.explanation: Confidence scores (from 0 to 1) show how reliable each value is, and grounding shows where it came from in the source, so low-confidence values can be routed to a person who can check them quickly.

questions.stem: A team is ingesting documents into a search index for retrieval-augmented generation and wants text that preserves headings and tables. Which output fits?
options: A list of bounding boxes only
A Markdown version of the content
questions.explanation: Content Understanding can output document content as Markdown, keeping structure such as sections and tables, which suits search and RAG. Structured JSON fields suit automation.

questions.stem: Which Content Understanding field method is supported for documents but not for images, audio, or video?
questions.explanation: Extract, which returns values exactly as they appear, is supported only for documents. For images, audio, and video, fields use Generate or Classify.

questions.stem: A retailer wants each product photo to return fields for product category and dominant color. How should it set up Content Understanding?
options: An image analyzer with classify or generate fields
A document analyzer with extract-only fields
A speech analyzer with a custom voice
A text analytics key phrase request
questions.explanation: An image analyzer with a field schema can classify the category from a fixed list and generate a description such as the dominant color.

questions.stem: What does Content Understanding need to power field generation and figure analysis?
options: A Speech resource in the same Azure region
A set of your own Foundry model deployments
An Azure AI Search index for every analyzer
A separate Azure Machine Learning training cluster
questions.explanation: Content Understanding uses large language and embedding models that you deploy in Foundry, and you configure which deployments it uses. It doesn't require a training cluster or a search index.

questions.stem: What does Content Understanding return for an audio file analyzed by an audio analyzer?
options: A neural voice trained on the speaker
A transcript, plus any fields you defined
Only a waveform image of the recording
A cleaned-up audio file with noise removed
questions.explanation: Audio analysis transcribes speech and then fills your schema, such as a summary, topics, or sentiment for a call.

questions.stem: A video analyzer should return separate descriptions for each scene of a training video. Which capability supports this?
questions.explanation: Segmentation divides content into logical sections, such as video scenes or document types, so fields can be generated for each segment. It's enabled through the analyzer's segmentation setting.

questions.stem: A call center wants every recorded call labeled with an overall sentiment from a fixed set of values. Which field method should the audio analyzer use?
questions.explanation: Classify picks a value from predefined categories, such as Positive, Neutral, or Negative, and works for audio. Extract applies only to documents.

questions.stem: During content extraction for video, what does Content Understanding do?
options: Generates a new video based on the transcript
Compresses the video for faster streaming
Converts the video into a sequence of text prompts
Transcribes speech and finds key visual elements
questions.explanation: For audio and video, content extraction transcribes speech and identifies key visual elements, such as keyframes, before field extraction runs.

questions.stem: How does a client app analyze a file with the Content Understanding REST API?
options: Call analyze on the analyzer, then poll for results
Stream the file to a Speech recognizer and read the text
Send the file to the Foundry playground through a browser
Upload the file to the model catalog and wait for an email
questions.explanation: Analysis is asynchronous: the app calls analyze for a specific analyzer ID, gets an operation location in the response, and polls it until the result is ready.

questions.stem: Which Azure resource hosts Content Understanding?
questions.explanation: Content Understanding is a Foundry Tool available as part of the Microsoft Foundry resource, and it uses model deployments in that resource.

questions.stem: What does an analyze request specify so the service knows which schema and settings to apply?
questions.explanation: Each analyze call targets an analyzer by its ID — a prebuilt analyzer or a custom one you created — which determines the extraction settings and fields.

questions.stem: A mailroom app receives a mix of invoices, receipts, and contracts. How can Content Understanding route each to the right extraction?
options: Classify each document, then use the matching analyzer
Send every document to a speech analyzer first
Use one extract-only field for all three document types
Ask users to rename files before uploading them
questions.explanation: Classification categorizes documents (and can split multi-document files) and routes each to the analyzer for that type, so each gets the right fields.

questions.stem: Which Content Understanding output suits an automation workflow that writes values into a database?
options: JSON that matches the field schema
A thumbnail image of each document page
An audio summary read by a neural voice
Markdown with headings and tables preserved
questions.explanation: Field extraction returns structured JSON aligned with your schema, with confidence and grounding, which code can map directly to database columns. Markdown suits search and RAG.
